# The Slow Work of Extraction

## Scripture

“But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, self-control; against such things there is no law.” — Galatians 5:22–23

## Reflection

Good coffee refuses to be rushed. The bean is roasted slowly, the grounds bloom, and the pour-over releases its flavor one patient drop at a time. Push the water through too fast and you get something thin and bitter—technically coffee, but not what it was meant to be. Extraction cannot be forced.

The fruit of the Spirit grows the same way. Paul doesn't list these qualities as achievements to manufacture by willpower; he calls them fruit. Fruit ripens. It takes soil, sun, and time. You cannot command patience into existence at 7 a.m. any more than you can hurry a roast without scorching it. What you can do is stay in the process—remain connected to the Vine, keep showing up to the ordinary means of grace, and let the Spirit do the slow work of drawing character out of you.

This is strangely freeing. Your job is not to extract your own goodness by grinding harder. Your job is to abide, and to trust that the One who began a good work is patient enough to finish it. Some mornings the brew is rich; some mornings it's weak and you feel spiritually flavorless. Neither morning changes the character of the Roaster. He is not in a hurry, and He is not wasting a single drop.

## Prayer

Father, we confess our impatience with Your slow work in us. Teach us to abide rather than strive, trusting You to ripen Your fruit in our lives in Your perfect time. In Jesus' name, amen.

## One-Line Application

Abide today; let the Spirit handle the extraction.
